llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究高熵合金的激光熔化制备与强化，未涉及生物医用植入物或应力遮挡问题。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address biomedical implants, porous structures for stress shielding, fatigue, surface roughness, or osseointegration; it focuses on high-entropy alloy precipitation strengthening without any biomedical context.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种通过选区激光熔化原位合金化和后热处理强化的高熵合金。
summary_zh.method: 采用选区激光熔化原位合金化，随后进行后热处理实现析出强化。
summary_zh.result: 获得了具有优异力学性能的析出强化高熵合金。
summary_zh.validation: 通过力学测试（拉伸、硬度等）验证强化效果。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloy using selective laser melting in-situ alloying and subsequent heat treatment.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting was employed for in-situ alloying, followed by post-heat treatment to induce precipitation strengthening.
summary_en.result: The alloy achieved improved mechanical properties due to precipitation strengthening.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing including tensile and hardness measurements validated the strengthening effect.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文聚焦于SLM多孔股骨柄的设计与性能预测，但未直接量化应力遮挡或微动，属于间接相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify stress shielding in Gruen zones or report micromotion values with contact/friction modeling; it lacks comparison between intact and implanted femur.

summary_zh.motivation: 设计并预测多孔股骨柄的力学性能，以优化植入物固定。
summary_zh.method: 利用选择性激光熔化技术制备多孔结构，结合有限元分析预测性能。
summary_zh.result: 多孔结构可降低刚度并改善应力分布，但未直接比较完整与植入股骨。
summary_zh.validation: 通过力学测试验证多孔试件的弹性模量和强度。

summary_en.motivation: To design a porous femoral stem with tailored mechanical properties to reduce stress shielding and improve implant longevity.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting (SLM) was used to fabricate porous structures, and finite element analysis predicted the mechanical performance of the stem.
summary_en.result: The porous design reduced stem stiffness and altered stress distribution, but no direct comparison of intact vs. implanted femur was performed.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical compression tests validated the elastic modulus and yield strength of the porous specimens.

papers.title: Levitational 3D Bioassembly and Density‐Based Spatial Coding of Levitoids
papers.abstract: Abstract Self‐assembly of cells into functional bioarchitectures with microscale spatial topographies are prevalent in nature. Despite the advances to recapitulate the native‐like microenvironment in vitro,fabrication of soft living materials with a deterministic control on the composition, functionality, and geometry, is still challenging. Here, a versatile, paramagnetically tunable, levitational biofabrication technique within a ring‐magnet system, RM‐LEV, is developed to assemble single cells or heterogeneous multicellular living architectures in a scaffold‐free manner. The self‐assembly and contactless biofabrication of multiple cell types into 3D multicellular “levitospheres” is demonstrated, where cellular positions are guided by levitation and density, simultaneously. Inherent density and diamagnetism of different cell types are leveraged to manipulate the geometry and self‐assembly of levitospheres into larger complex 3D structures, termed as “levitoids”. This approach is further applied to manipulate, position, and culture levitoids within a 3D hydrogel matrix under levitation, which preserves their viability and functionality. Thus, this study provides a foundation to create spatially heterogeneous 3D cellular assemblies with density‐coded bio‐architectures—which is not previously realized using magnetic levitation. This density‐based coding approach can be beneficial to study the cross‐talk between different cell types within spheroids and organoids, and be broadly applied to 3D bioprinting, tissue engineering, cancer, and neuroscience research.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发不受限的细胞自组装方法以构建复杂三维结构。
summary_zh.method: 利用环形磁铁构建顺磁可调悬浮生物组装系统。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a versatile, scaffold-free biofabrication technique for assembling cells into complex 3D architectures with spatial control.
summary_en.method: A paramagnetically tunable levitational biofabrication system using a ring magnet (RM-LEV) to guide cell self-assembly via density and diamagnetism.
summary_en.result: The system produces multicellular 'levitoids' with density-coded spatial organization, maintaining viability in hydrogel matrices.
summary_en.validation: In vitro culture and viability assays confirm functionality of levitated cell assemblies.

papers.title: 3D Bioprinting Using Hydrogels: Cell Inks and Tissue Engineering Applications.
papers.abstract: 3D bioprinting is transforming tissue engineering in medicine by providing novel methods that are precise and highly customizable to create biological tissues. The selection of a "cell ink", a printable formulation, is an integral part of adapting 3D bioprinting processes to allow for process optimization and customization related to the target tissue. Bioprinting hydrogels allows for tailorable material, physical, chemical, and biological properties of the cell ink and is suited for biomedical applications. Hydrogel-based cell ink formulations are a promising option for the variety of techniques with which bioprinting can be achieved. In this review, we will examine some of the current hydrogel-based cell inks used in bioprinting, as well as their use in current and proposed future bioprinting methods. We will highlight some of the biological applications and discuss the development of new hydrogels and methods that can incorporate the completed print into the tissue or organ of interest.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文是水凝胶细胞墨水在3D生物打印中的综述，完全不涉及AI或智能控制。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a pure materials review with no AI integration, no experimental validation of AI models, and no autonomous decision-making workflow.

summary_zh.method: 文献综述，分析不同水凝胶配方及其打印特性。
summary_zh.result: 总结了适用于生物打印的水凝胶种类及其组织工程应用。
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，为综述性总结。

summary_en.motivation: To review current hydrogel-based cell inks for 3D bioprinting and their role in tissue engineering.
summary_en.method: A literature review examining various hydrogel formulations, printability, and biological properties.
summary_en.result: The review summarizes existing hydrogel cell inks and their applications in creating tissue constructs.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; the paper is a theoretical review.
